text.56_Daf, 17_Line, 0_Comment: Inside of the "Hey"- The inside leg
text.57_Daf, 2_Line, 0_Comment: Crowns: Such as the markings of a Torah scroll.
text.57_Daf, 2_Line, 1_Comment: Who is preventing You from [leaving alone] what You wrote, that You need to add the crowns to the [letters].
text.57_Daf, 3_Line, 0_Comment: Arrived at a matter that needed explanation.
text.57_Daf, 3_Line, 1_Comment: His mind was put at ease [the mind] of Moshe; since he spoke in his name - even though he had not yet received [the Torah].
text.57_Daf, 4_Line, 0_Comment: In makkulin: A place of butchers. They were weighing his flesh, as it said in Berakhot (61b) that they combed his flesh with steel combs (and ripped it off).
text.64_Daf, 4_Line, 0_Comment: He made it like a bolt.  That he fixed it and inserted it into the doorpost/threshold. Like a bolt that carpenters push into the wall. Like This:
text.64_Daf, 4_Line, 1_Comment: It is invalid — because the commandment is to place it lengthwise along the doorpost like this. A bolt of the type called kavila (this is a french word describing a type of bolt)*.
text.64_Daf, 4_Line, 2_Comment: That doorway through which Rebbi would enter the study hall — it was a small doorway that Rebbi had near his place, and he would enter and exit through it so that he would not trouble his students to stand before him if he passed in front of them.
text.64_Daf, 4_Line, 3_Comment: 'Istrevhu' — this is the place where the thigh and the leg join, and it is measured while standing.  Like this is valid.
text.64_Daf, 4_Line, 4_Comment: He made it like a peg - bolt of carpenters, like this, is invalid.  Another interpretation of 'Istravehu' (a leg), just like the place that connects the leg and the foot and the leg is upright going up and the foot is sideways like this.  This did Rebbi place the mezuzah and it's valid since one end is standing straight.
text.70_Daf, 0_Line, 0_Comment: Between the placing of one of the Tefillin and the other one - Between that of the hand and that of the head. He spoke before he placed on the one of the head.
text.70_Daf, 1_Line, 0_Comment: To lay on - Because he starts laying with that of the hand.
text.70_Daf, 1_Line, 1_Comment: The precept of Tefillin - Because now he finishes the precept.
text.70_Daf, 2_Line, 0_Comment: If he did not talk - He only blesses on that of the hand alone.
text.70_Daf, 2_Line, 1_Comment: If he talked he says two blessings - Like Rav Chiya sent.
text.80_Daf, 17_Line, 0_Comment: At that time - at the time when the corpse is dressed.
text.80_Daf, 17_Line, 1_Comment: We certainly affix - we put tzitzit [on the shroud] because were they not attached, it would be like mocking the dead. As we have learned, the dead are exempt from mitzvot.
text.81_Daf, 12_Line, 0_Comment: 1) Meshuleshet - How much should the strings hang from the tied part
text.85_Daf, 9_Line, 0_Comment: "Seven times a day" - tefillin on the head and on the arm, this is two, and four tzitzit, and a mezuzah, this is seven
text.195_Daf, 17_Line, 1_Comment: From here we infer that the middle position is commendable - regarding three that read Torah on Mondays and Thursdays, and we say in Megillah 21b: "we do not read any less than ten verses. And Rabbi Yochana says: the middle [alyiah] is preferable, and that is four verses, and the others are three and three.
text.197_Daf, 0_Line, 0_Comment: For the withdrawal of Torah - for example one who withdraws from learning Torah to escort the deceased and for ushering in the bride this is the foundation of Torah meaning to say he receives reward as if he is sitting and learning as it says that you have broken and it does not say it with anger implicating that G-d agreed with his action when he eliminated Torah when breaking the tablets since he intended for the good
